headline: Quiet one-day window; 10y at 5.18% while IG spreads hold at 0.79%
verdict: The window since yesterday's brief is one day, a Saturday, and it brought no material build-out news. The refreshed data moved only rates. The 10y is 5.18% (2026-09-24), +24bp on the week and +54bp on the month, while IG OAS holds at 0.79% and BBB at 0.97%. The thesis stands: spend is accelerating (+86.5% YoY in 2026Q2), it is funded from outside (T4Q capex/OCF 82%), and the cost shows up in Treasuries, not spreads.
what_changed: The 10y Treasury is 5.18% as of 2026-09-24, up from the 5.11% (2026-09-23) quoted last brief: +24bp on the week and +54bp on the month; the 2y is 4.87%, +20bp on the week.
HY OAS widened 10bp on the week to 2.80% while IG (+1bp) and BBB (+2bp) barely moved.

spend.claim: Capex is still accelerating; nothing in the window changes that.
spend.body: Unchanged: no guidance changes in the window, and combined capex was still $181.5bn in 2026Q2, +86.5% YoY.

funding.claim: Funding costs keep rising through Treasuries, not IG spreads.
funding.body: Only rates moved. The 10y is 5.18% (2026-09-24), +24bp on the week and +102bp on the year; the 2y is 4.87%, +20bp on the week. The term premium is 0.96% as of 2026-09-18, with no newer print. Spreads have not followed: IG OAS is 0.79% (+1bp on the week), BBB 0.97% (+2bp). HY OAS widened 10bp to 2.80%, the only credit series that moved. No new hyperscaler, Oracle or neocloud deals or ratings actions in the window. Trailing capex is still 82% of operating cash flow.

receivers.claim: Suppliers are still booking the money; the next test is Micron on September 30.
receivers.body: Unchanged: no supplier results in the window. NVDA was +105.9% YoY in 2026Q2, and Micron's fiscal Q4 (June–August) report on September 30 is the next read on memory.

evidence.text: Micron reports fiscal Q4 on September 30, 2026

macro.claim: IT investment is still carrying about a third of GDP growth; productivity has not stepped up.
macro.body: Unchanged: no GDP, productivity or CPI release in the window; IT equipment plus software still account for 0.70pp of 2.12% average growth over four quarters, or 33%.

market.claim: The market still pays suppliers and not the spenders as a group.
market.body: Unchanged: no new news in the window. Over a year, SMH/SPY is 159.9 against 81.2 for the hyperscalers, and XLU/SPY is 80.3.

tripwires.name: Spend slows
tripwires.reading: Combined capex +86.5% YoY in 2026Q2 (data/summary.md); no guidance cuts in the window.

tripwires.name: Cash burn
tripwires.reading: T4Q capex/OCF 82% in 2026Q2, up from 75% in 2026Q1, against a 100% line (data/summary.md).

tripwires.name: IG spreads wake up
tripwires.reading: IG OAS 0.79%, BBB OAS 0.97% on 2026-09-24, against 1.10% / 1.30% (FRED, data/summary.md).

tripwires.name: Weak link cracks
tripwires.reading: Oracle BBB- at S&P since July, one notch above high yield; no rating action or CoreWeave credit event found in the window.

tripwires.name: Suppliers roll over
tripwires.reading: NVDA revenue +105.9% YoY in 2026Q2 (data/summary.md); Micron reports September 30.

tripwires.name: Rates bite
tripwires.reading: 10y 5.18% on 2026-09-24, +54bp in a month, against 5.50%; term premium 0.96% (2026-09-18) against 1.25% (FRED, data/summary.md).

tripwires.name: Payoff shows up (bullish)
tripwires.reading: Productivity +2.2% over four quarters (quarter starting 2026-04-01), down from +2.9% (data/summary.md).

thesis_suggestions: Tripwires: IG OAS is +4bp on the year while the 10y is +102bp and HY OAS +10bp on the week alone. T3 may trip only after T4 does. Consider adding a tripwire on HY OAS or on Oracle/neocloud bond spreads, so stress in the weak links shows up before the IG index moves.

sources.title: Micron Technology to Report Fiscal Fourth Quarter Results on September 30, 2026
Oracle stock shrugs off S&P downgrade to BBB- (Yahoo Finance)
